headline: Study and Serve at the Royal Military College

sections.title: What is the Royal Military College?
sections.content:
The Royal Military College of Canada (RMC) in Kingston, Ontario, is the country's military university. Officer cadets study for a bachelor's degree while training as future officers of the Canadian Armed Forces. Degrees are offered in engineering, science, and military and strategic studies, and all cadets live on campus in co-ed residences.

Most undergraduate cadets enter through the Regular Officer Training Plan (ROTP). The Government of Canada covers full tuition, books and uniforms, and officer cadets also receive a monthly salary while they study. In return, graduates owe a period of service as commissioned officers.

sections.title: ROTP admission requirements
sections.content:
ROTP is open to Canadian citizens. Applicants need a minimum average of 75%, with at least 75% in prerequisite courses, and a grade range of 75 to 80% is typical for successful candidates. Early conditional offers may go to applicants presenting marks of 85% or higher, including prerequisites. Strong grades in mathematics and sciences matter most for engineering programs.

Applicants apply through a Canadian Forces Recruiting Centre, choosing ROTP as their education plan and RMC as their preferred institution. The process includes the Canadian Armed Forces aptitude test (CFAT), a medical exam and an interview. The ROTP application deadline is January 31, 2027, and candidates are advised to apply in their final year of high school.

sections.title: Degrees and campus life
sections.content:
RMC offers four-year degrees including Bachelor of Engineering in mechanical, electrical, civil, aeronautical and chemical engineering, Bachelor of Science in mathematics, computer science, physics, chemistry and space science, and Bachelor of Arts in military and strategic studies. All ROTP officer cadets must live in residence, with single rooms preferred in senior years.

Campus life combines academics, military training and sport. Cadets follow a structured daily routine, take part in leadership training, and build the discipline expected of officers. On-campus dining is provided, and cadets take part in intramural and varsity athletics throughout the year.

sections.title: Graduate studies and international applicants
sections.content:
RMC also runs graduate programs, including Master of Applied Science, Master of Engineering, Master of Arts in War Studies and Master of Public Administration. Civilian graduate enrolment is open to Canadian citizens or permanent residents, with exceptional international admits considered case by case, mainly for engineering research and war studies.

Undergraduate seats are effectively closed to international civilians because they run only through ROTP. International students interested in a defence-adjacent bachelor's degree should look at civilian programs at universities such as Queen's, Toronto, McGill or Carleton, then apply to RMC at the graduate level.

faqs.q: What grades do you need for RMC Canada?
faqs.a: You need a minimum average of 75%, with at least 75% in prerequisite courses. The typical grade range for successful ROTP applicants is 75 to 80%. Early conditional offers may go to applicants with 85% or higher, including prerequisites. Strong mathematics and science grades matter most for engineering programs.

faqs.q: Is RMC Canada free for officer cadets?
faqs.a: Yes, under the Regular Officer Training Plan the Government of Canada covers tuition, books and uniforms, and officer cadets also receive a salary while studying. In return, graduates commit to a period of service as commissioned officers in the Canadian Armed Forces after graduation.

faqs.q: When is the ROTP application deadline?
faqs.a: The ROTP application deadline is January 31, 2027. Candidates should apply as soon as they can once they begin their final year of high school. Applications go through a Canadian Forces Recruiting Centre, with the aptitude test, medical exam and interview following the initial application.

Undergraduate seats are effectively closed to international civilians because they run only through the Regular Officer Training Plan, which requires Canadian citizenship. International applicants can be considered case by case for graduate research programs, mainly in engineering and war studies, with a supervisor's approval.
